title: Motor Milestones: Rolling to Crawling
hook: In the first year babies move through a rough sequence — rolling, sitting, crawling, pulling to stand — but the timing varies widely, and ranges matter more than exact dates.
key_points: Milestones are ranges, not deadlines: many babies sit around 6 months and many crawl between 7 and 10 months.
Not every baby crawls in the classic way — some scoot, shuffle, or skip straight to pulling up.
Supervised tummy time while awake builds the neck, shoulder, and core strength behind these skills.
Trust patterns over single dates; raise it with a pediatrician if a baby misses a whole cluster of milestones.
content_html: Across the first year, babies generally build motor skills in a loose order: lifting the head, rolling over, sitting, crawling, and pulling up to stand. It's tempting to treat these as a checklist with fixed dates, but the healthier framing is ranges — for example, many babies sit with support around six months and crawl somewhere between seven and ten months.
extra_html: There's also more than one normal path. Plenty of babies never crawl in the textbook hands-and-knees way; they scoot on their bottom, commando-crawl, or go straight to pulling up. What helps across the board is supervised tummy time while your baby is awake, which builds the strength behind every later skill. Reference points like the CDC's milestone checklists are useful, but they're a guide, not a verdict — patterns over time matter more than any single date, and a pediatrician is the right person to ask if a baby seems to miss a whole cluster of milestones. This is general educational information.

related.title: Starting Solid Foods
related.hook: Most babies are ready for their first solid foods at around six months — alongside continued breast milk or formula, not instead of it.

related.title: Tummy Time: Back to Sleep, Tummy to Play
related.hook: The same babies who must sleep on their backs need time on their tummies while awake — it builds the strength behind rolling and crawling, and helps keep the back of the head from flattening.

flashcards.prompt: How should developmental milestone ages best be understood?

choices.text: As ranges, since healthy babies vary widely in timing
As fixed deadlines every baby must hit
As identical for all babies of the same weight

flashcards.explanation_html: Milestones describe typical ranges. Patterns over time matter more than any single date — though missing a cluster is worth a pediatrician's review.

flashcards.prompt: Why is supervised tummy time useful for motor development?
flashcards.back_html: It builds the neck, shoulder, and core strength babies need to roll, sit, and eventually crawl. Always do it while the baby is awake and watched.
